newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ coalition tables "sound, compassionate" budget.
newsitem.headline: NZ coalition tables "sound, compassionate" budget.

text.p: New Zealand's centre-right coalition government delivered its maiden budget on Thursday, detailing plans for NZ$5.0 billion ($3.43 billion) of spending on social priorities and projecting continued budget surpluses.

However, as ministers had warned in the last week, the forecast surplus for the 1997/98 year was slashed by a current economic lull and one-off factors to just NZ$1.5 billion versus a $3.3 billion forecast made in March.

Treasurer Winston Peters, whose build-up to the budget has been clouded by a series of scandals involving members of his junior government party New Zealand First, called the budget "sound and compassionate".

He rejected criticism of the Treasury's forecasts for a surge in economic growth from a low of 2.5 percent in the year to March 1997 to 4.2 percent in the year to March 1999, which economists said appeared over optimistic.
"I think we are being conservative here, and I think that is good in the first year of a three year term," he told reporters.

Prime Minister Jim Bolger stressed that the budget also sought to restore certainty to the business sector through pledges to remove all tariffs by 2010, to increase competition in electricity generation and to consider selling non-strategic state-owned enterprises.
